text: Two isolated metallic solid spheres of radii $\mathrm{R}$ and $2\mathrm{R}$ are charged such that both have same charge density $σ$. The spheres are then connected by a thin conducting wire. If the new charge density of the bigger sphere is $σ^{'}$. The ratio $\frac{σ^{'}}{σ}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Charge on a metallic sphere resides on its surface, so $σ$ is the surface charge density of each sphere.

Initial charges: $Q_{1}=σ(4πR^{2})$ and $Q_{2}=σ4π(2R)^{2}=16πR^{2}σ$, so the total charge is $Q=20πR^{2}σ$.

After connection both spheres are at the same potential:

$\dfrac{kQ_{1}^{'}}{R}=\dfrac{kQ_{2}^{'}}{2R}\Rightarrow Q_{2}^{'}=2Q_{1}^{'}$

So the bigger sphere gets two-thirds of the total charge:

$Q_{2}^{'}=\dfrac{2}{3}\times 20πR^{2}σ=\dfrac{40}{3}πR^{2}σ$

$σ^{'}=\dfrac{Q_{2}^{'}}{4π(2R)^{2}}=\dfrac{40πR^{2}σ}{3\times 16πR^{2}}=\dfrac{5}{6}σ\Rightarrow \dfrac{σ^{'}}{σ}=\dfrac{5}{6}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
If the gravitational field in the space is given as $\left (-\frac{K}{r^{2}}\right )$. Taking the reference point to be at $\mathrm{r}=2\mathrm{cm}$ 
with gravitational potential $\mathrm{V}=10\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{kg}$. Find the gravitational potential at $\mathrm{r}=3\mathrm{cm}$ in SI unit (Given, that $\mathrm{K}=6\mathrm{Jcm}/\mathrm{kg}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The field and potential are related by $E=-\dfrac{dV}{dr}$, so $dV=-Edr=\dfrac{K}{r^{2}}dr$.

Integrating from the reference point $r=2\text{cm}$ to $r=3\text{cm}$:

$V_{3}-V_{2}=\int\limits _{2}^{3}\dfrac{K}{r^{2}}dr=K\left [-\dfrac{1}{r}\right ]_{2}^{3}=K\left (\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{1}{3}\right )=\dfrac{K}{6}$

With $r$ in cm, $\dfrac{1}{6}$ is in $\text{cm}^{-1}$, and $K=6\text{J cm kg}^{-1}$:

$V_{3}-V_{2}=\dfrac{6}{6}=1\text{J kg}^{-1}$

$V_{3}=10+1=11\text{J kg}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
In an experiment for estimating the value of focal length of converging mirror, image of an object placed at $40\mathrm{cm}$ from the pole of the mirror is formed at distance $120\mathrm{cm}$ from the pole of the mirror. solution.body:
$\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}$ ...... (1)

$\Rightarrow -\frac{1}{f^{2}}df=-\frac{1}{v^{2}}dv-\frac{1}{u^{2}}du$

$\Rightarrow \frac{df}{f^{2}}=\frac{dv}{v^{2}}+\frac{du}{u^{2}}$ ..... (2)

$\Rightarrow k=32$

text: The general displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is $x=A\sin ωt$. Let T be its time period. The slope of its potential energy (U) - time (t) curve will be maximum when $t=\frac{T}{β}$. The value of $β$ is $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $x=A\sin ωt$, the potential energy is

$U=\dfrac{1}{2}mω^{2}x^{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}mω^{2}A^{2}\sin ^{2}ωt$

By the chain rule, $\dfrac{d}{dt}\left (\sin ^{2}ωt\right )=2\sin ωt\cos ωt\times ω=ω\sin 2ωt$, so

$\dfrac{dU}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{2}mω^{3}A^{2}\sin 2ωt$

The slope is maximum when $\sin 2ωt=1$, first at $2ωt=\dfrac{π}{2}$, i.e. $t=\dfrac{π}{4ω}$.

With $ω=\dfrac{2π}{T}$:

$t=\dfrac{πT}{4\times 2π}=\dfrac{T}{8}\Rightarrow β=8$

Hence, the answer is 8.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

solution.body:
From the circuit :

$V_{A}-iR-\frac{Ldi}{dt}-12=V_{B}$

$\Rightarrow V_{A}-V_{B}=2\times 12+6(-1)+12$ volts

$=30$ volts

text: In a screw gauge, there are 100 divisions on the circular scale and the main scale moves by $0.5\mathrm{mm}$ on a complete rotation of the circular scale. The zero of circular scale lies 6 divisions below the line of graduation when two studs are brought in contact with each other. When a wire is placed between the studs, 4 linear scale divisions are clearly visible while $46^{\text{th}}$ division the circular scale coincide with the reference line. The diameter of the wire is $______________$ $\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{mm}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Pitch $=0.5\text{mm}$ and the circular scale has 100 divisions, so the least count is

$\text{LC}=\dfrac{0.5\text{mm}}{100}=0.005\text{mm}$

With the studs in contact, the zero of the circular scale is 6 divisions below the reference line, so the reference line already reads $+6$ divisions: the zero error is positive, $e=+6\times 0.005=+0.03\text{mm}$.

The linear scale advances by the pitch, $0.5\text{mm}$ per division, so 4 visible divisions give $\text{LSR}=4\times 0.5=2.0\text{mm}$.

Circular scale reading $=46\times 0.005=0.23\text{mm}$, so the observed reading is $2.0+0.23=2.23\text{mm}$.

$d=2.23\text{mm}-0.03\text{mm}=2.20\text{mm}=220\times 10^{-2}\text{mm}$

Hence, the answer is 220.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text: A point source of light is placed at the centre of curvature of a hemispherical surface. The source emits a power of $24\mathrm{W}$. The radius of curvature of hemisphere is $10\mathrm{cm}$ and the inner surface is completely reflecting. The force on the hemisphere due to the light falling on it is $____________$ $\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{N}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Every ray from the source at the centre of curvature travels along a radius, so it strikes the hemisphere normally at every point. With source power $p_{0}=24\text{W}$ and radius $R$, the intensity on the surface is

$I=\dfrac{p_{0}}{4πR^{2}}$

For normal incidence on a perfectly reflecting surface the radiation pressure is $P=\dfrac{2I}{c}$, so an element $dA$ receives a force $PdA$ along the outward radius.


[IMG]

By symmetry about the axis, the force components perpendicular to the axis cancel, and only the axial components $PdA\cos θ$ add, where $θ$ is the angle between the radius and the axis. Since $dA\cos θ$ is the projection of $dA$ on the plane of the rim, $\int dA\cos θ=πR^{2}$, the area of the rim circle, not the curved area $2πR^{2}$.

$F=\dfrac{2I}{c}πR^{2}=\dfrac{2p_{0}}{4πR^{2}c}πR^{2}=\dfrac{p_{0}}{2c}$

$F=\dfrac{24}{2\times 3\times 10^{8}}=4\times 10^{-8}\text{N}$

Hence, the answer is 4.

text: A capacitor of capacitance $900μ\mathrm{F}$ is charged by a $100\mathrm{V}$ battery. The capacitor is disconnected from the battery and connected to another uncharged identical capacitor such that one plate of uncharged capacitor connected to positive plate and another plate of uncharged capacitor connected to negative plate of the charged capacitor. The loss of energy in this process is measured as $x\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{J}$. The value of $x$ is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$U_{i}=\frac{1}{2}CV^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\times 900\times 10^{-6}\times 100^{2}=4.5$ J

As the other capacitor is identical therefore charge is equally divided and potential difference across the capacitors becomes half. So

$U_{f}=\frac{1}{2}2C\left (\frac{V}{2}\right )^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times 900\times 10^{-6}\left (\frac{100}{2}\right )^{2}$

$=\frac{9}{4}$ J = 2.25 J

So, loss in energy $\Delta U_{loss}=U_{i}-U_{f}$

= 2.25 J

= 225 $\times$ 10${}^{-2}$ J
